display.purpose: Hero headlines and section titles. Cormorant Garamond carries the authority of the practice name itself. Reserve for the single most significant statement on a page.

headline.purpose: Sub-section headers, card titles, portal section headings. Still Cormorant; more intimate than Display scale.

body.purpose: All body copy. DM Sans at comfortable reading size. Capped at 65–75ch via --text-w: 740px. Comfortable reading is a non-negotiable system commitment.

label.purpose: Eyebrow labels, navigation links, button text, status badges. DM Sans, uppercase, wide letter-spacing — the voice of official process.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Staggered scroll-reveal on .r elements. translateY(18px) → translateY(0), opacity 0 → 1. Five delay steps: 0.08s increments up to 0.40s.

motion.name: color-transition
motion.purpose: Default easing for color, background, and border-color state changes (hover, active). Never transition layout properties.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Desktop to tablet: nav link padding reduces, some two-column layouts adjust.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Tablet to mobile: navigation hamburger appears, desktop nav links and actions hidden.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Mobile: section padding reduces to 5rem/1.25rem, footer stacks and centre-aligns.

components.name: Primary Button

narrative.overview:
This is a serious professional firm. Every element carries the weight of documented process and legal precision. The design communicates that a real expert operates here — not a platform, not a portal, not a startup with a gradient — a practice that has guided hundreds of clients through the same procedural journey and knows every obstacle. When a referred prospect lands on any Visa Forte surface, the design's job is not to convince from zero; it is to confirm what they already believe.

The visual language is grounded in restraint. Prussian blue anchors every surface in authority. Saffron appears as a precision instrument — sparingly, on the most credible, the most actionable, the most important. Pearl grounds the experience in warmth, far from clinical white. Nothing is rounded; nothing floats; nothing animates for its own sake. This is the design equivalent of a firm handshake.

The system explicitly rejects generic SaaS aesthetics, cheap immigration portal styling, over-designed agency excess, and old-school legal firm stiffness. It also refuses anything that causes visual fatigue — comfortable reading is a design feature, not an afterthought.
keyCharacteristics: Zero border-radius throughout: square corners signal seriousness, not consumer softness
Flat elevation: authority comes from color and type, never from shadow depth
Saffron as a precision instrument: used on ≤10% of any screen; its rarity is the point
Pearl canvas: warm off-white, never clinical white, always approachable
Cormorant Garamond for display only: the serif carries authority; DM Sans carries clarity
Uppercase labels and buttons: the visual language of official process and documentation

rules.name: The Saffron Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Saffron appears on ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is precisely why it commands attention. Over-use collapses the contrast hierarchy and makes CTAs invisible in noise.

rules.name: The No-White Rule
rules.body: Never use pure #fff or #000. Pearl (#F8F4EE) is the lightest neutral; Prussian (#0C2340) is the darkest. Every color is tinted toward the brand hue.

rules.name: The Serif Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Cormorant Garamond is reserved for display and headline roles exclusively. Never use it for body copy, navigation, or any UI element at or below 1rem.

rules.name: The Uppercase Protocol
rules.body: Labels, navigation, buttons, and eyebrow text are always uppercase with wide letter-spacing (0.10–0.28em). The visual language of official documentation. Do not undercut it with mixed case in UI contexts.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. No box-shadow on buttons, cards, inputs, or containers. Depth is earned through color contrast, not shadow illusion.

dos: Do use Cormorant Garamond for display (≥1.5rem) and DM Sans for everything else. The serif ceiling is strict and non-negotiable.
Do place the Saffron Rule (40px × 2px, #C97B1E) between the eyebrow/headline and body content in every major section.
Do display 'Engineered for Passage.' as the permanent nav tagline in Saffron (#C97B1E). Never alter, never omit.
Do keep border-radius at 0px on all interactive elements: buttons, inputs, cards, badges, chips.
Do use uppercase with letter-spacing (≥0.10em) for all navigation links, button labels, and eyebrow text.
Do set body copy on Pearl (#F8F4EE) with Ink (#1A2B3C) text at comfortable line lengths (max 65–75ch).
Do keep Saffron usage to ≤10% of any given screen.
Do use the flat elevation model throughout. No box-shadow on buttons, cards, or containers.
Do include prefers-reduced-motion overrides on all .r reveal animations. WCAG 2.1 AA compliance is required.
donts: Don't use gradient hero sections, gradient text (background-clip: text), or hero-metric templates (big number + small label + gradient accent).
Don't apply cheap immigration portal patterns: blue-and-white government-adjacent styling, stock flag photography, poor contrast, typographic negligence.
Don't add parallax effects, decorative floating blobs, neon splashes, excessive motion, or cursor effects.
Don't use old-school legal firm aesthetics: gold serif wordmarks on dark navy, tombstone-style layouts, Latin language, cold formality.
Don't use any border-radius on interactive elements. Not 4px. Not 2px. Not 1px. Zero.
Don't add box-shadow to buttons, cards, or containers. Flat is a deliberate system choice.
Don't use Saffron as a large-surface background color. It belongs on rules, highlights, badges, CTAs, and hover states only.
Don't use pure #fff or #000. Pearl is the lightest neutral. Prussian is the darkest.
Don't set body copy in Cormorant Garamond. The Serif Ceiling Rule is absolute.
Don't design anything that causes visual fatigue. If a user squints or fights the layout, it has failed.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a decorative colored stripe on cards or alerts.
Don't use glassmorphism decoratively. The nav blur is a structural necessity; everywhere else it is prohibited.
